Mark — attaching our completed response pack (summary and artifacts) and answering the Appendix B items inline below. Attachment list is at the bottom.

SHORT SUMMARY (TL;DR):
- Controller/Processor: Customer is the controller for customer data stored/processed in-customer VPC; Redwood is processor only for any optional managed services. Contract language and a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) will be provided.
- Telemetry: For Private deployments we ship a lightweight heartbeating and billing telemetry agent. Telemetry data collection can be set to fully local (no egress) or to a managed control plane. When configured to managed control plane, retained telemetry fields are limited to: instance health metrics, aggregated token counts used for billing, and anonymized error traces (no request payloads). Default retention is 30 days; retention policies may be extended/shortened by contract.
- Operator access & residency: By default, operator access to customer private infrastructure is disabled. Where remote operator support is contracted, access is gated by:
  * Explicit authorized operator list (customer-managed allowlist)
  * Time-limited ephemeral credentials (short-lived certs) and SSO w/ customer IdP
  * Background checks and security questionnaires for any named operator accounts (we provide attestations).
  * Residency: we can contract geographic residency controls (e.g., operator actions must be performed by staff within the US/EU) — this is an enterprise option and documented in the SOW.
- Patching & updates in air-gapped/offline installs: Our offline update mechanism uses signed update bundles with SHA-256 checksums and a chain-of-trust anchored to a Redwood code-signing certificate. For air-gapped installs, we provide a signed bundle and verification steps; we also publish SBOM and signature metadata. Emergency patching can be performed via customer-approved operator-run offline bundles or via a remote-assisted patch session controlled by the customer.

APPENDIX B RESPONSES (selected, condensed):
2. Dataflow & legal boundary:
- Data ingress: Customer requests enter the customer VPC and are processed there; if prefix caching is enabled, keys for caching remain inside the customer network.
- Optional managed control plane: only metadata (instance id, billable token totals, anonymized health pings) flows to Redwood managed endpoints. We will provide a diagram showing these hops (attached).
- Legal boundary: DPA will identify the customer as controller and Redwood as processor; sub-processing (if any) will be disclosed in the DPA and requires customer consent for sensitive sub-processors.

4. Telemetry & logs:
- Types collected (managed mode): instance health metrics, token counters, anonymized stack traces, agent heartbeat.
- Types never collected: full user prompt/response content, PDF attachments, or PII parsed from payloads.
- Retention & access: default 30 days in managed mode, audited access via RBAC and logging. Local-only mode: telemetry stored on customer infra and not copied out.

7. Operator access & background checks:
- Background checks: we run role-appropriate checks for operators with escalation privileges; evidence of checks is available for review under NDA.
- Access model: customer primary, Redwood secondary (only when authorized). All operator actions are logged and reversible where possible.

EVIDENCE & ATTACHMENTS INCLUDED:
- Redwood_Private_Controls_FAQs.pdf (pdf) — narrative answers and sample contractual clauses
- Deployment_Dataflow_Diagram.png (png) — visual of in-VPC flows, optional managed control plane, KMS hops
- sample_audit_log_snippet.txt (text) — sanitized audit log showing operator actions (removed PII)

If you want, Naomi can draft DPA contract language specific to sections 2 and 4 for your legal team to review. Happy to prioritize that.
